newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk Nickel seeks trade finance from WestLB.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk Nickel seeks trade finance from WestLB.

text.p: Norilsk Nickel, seeking trade financing and extra cash, may sign a deal with Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale for a $100 million one-year loan to finance exports, a Norilsk spokesman said on Thursday.
Sergei Vetchinin said the deal could help RAO Norilsky Nikel 0#NKEL.RUO increase its metals exports, but without significantly affecting world prices.
"Of course we want to export more, but not in a way that will sharply move prices," he said.
He declined to elaborate, saying only that Norilsk was focusing on selling to end-users and cutting out intermediaries.
"There are technical ways allowing us to increase output which we are examining -- we may cooperate with other companies, like steel enterprises," he said.

He said that the WestLB credit, which the bank had offered but for which a formal agreement had not yet been signed, would technically go to Interrosimpex, Norilsk's new sole authorised exporter and foreign agent.

"What we wanted from Normaco, we are now getting from Interrosimpex," he said, referring to London-based Normaco Ltd, a Norilsk subsidiary which until July carried out most Norilsk export contracts before its functions were reorganised.
Vetchinin also said that a consortium of banks grouping ABN Amro, Banque Paribas, ING Bank and Chase Manhattan was also in talks with Norilsk and Interrosimpex on trade financing.
Norilsk, facing a cash crunch, is seeking ways to maximise profits from exports of nickel and copper.
Vetchinin said the bank credits would also be used to pay wage arrears and haul in consumer goods to company headquarters in the Arctic.

Russia's September output of nickel, most of it produced by Norilsk, was unchanged from August but 10 percent below year-ago levels, according to the State Statistics Committee. Output over January-September was four percent below year-ago levels.
September refined copper output fell 10 percent on August but was unchanged from 1995 levels. Refined copper output over January-September was four percent above year-ago levels.
Vetchinin and the committee declined to provide absolute production levels, but said 1996 nickel and copper output would probably be flat on 1995.
In 1995, the Norilsk group produced 180,100 tonnes of nickel and 338,700 tonnes of copper.
